links.outcome: Case performance of clinicians using ChatGPT versus own research on occupational medicine cases
links.effect: ChatGPT group did better on specific research questions (2.5 vs 1.8 hazardous substances, P=.01), but made fewer correct clinical decisions (report filed: 7 vs 14, P=.007; OR 6.00, 95% CI 1.54-23.36).
links.quote: However, clinical decisions, for example, whether an occupational disease report should be filed, were more often made correctly as a result of the participant's own research (n=29; eg, case 1: Should an occupational disease report be filed? Yes for 7 participants in the ChatGPT group vs 14 in their own research group; P=.007; odds ratio 6.00, 95% CI 1.54-23.36).

screen.reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating physicians and medical students solving simulated occupational medicine clinical vignettes using GPT-4 vs standard internet research tools.
